weekend.title: A key that outlived its memory
weekend.caption: The bank kept key 4471 for 24 hours. Worker A came back after 64, sent the same key, and the bank paid €50,000 a second time.

clock.title: Time moves only on Tick
clock.caption: The weekend as states. Only the two Tick steps move the dial, each by 12 hours; every other step happens inside a tick, and as many of them as you like fit in one.

timeout-guard.title: A timeout switches Forget on
timeout-guard.caption: A timeout switches an action on; it does not force it. From tick 2 the bank may forget key 4471 at any moment, or never, and from then on a resend may pay twice.

clock-bound.title: A short clock hides the weekend
clock-bound.caption: Each extra tick adds states. MaxTime 0 and 1 have no double payout because the clock never reaches the key’s 24 hours; from MaxTime 2 on, every clock contains the weekend.

two-worlds.title: Two worlds, one view from A
two-worlds.caption: A lost request and a lost reply. The bank differs, 0 transfers or 1, but worker A sees exactly the same thing in both: waiting, no reply.

stale-answer.title: True when written, false when read
stale-answer.caption: True when written, false when read. The bank answered “absent” while the payment was still in the network; by the time worker A read it, the money had moved and the key was gone.

deadline.title: The window must end before the key can
deadline.caption: Window 1 closes a tick before the bank may forget the key, so every request of the window that pays lands on it. Window 2 ends on the tick the key may vanish: same tick, either order.

fresh-answer.title: An absent from the wrong window
fresh-answer.caption: Both answers were written at tick 2. The first came after the first window closed and was right to trust; the other was read in the second window, and only the check m.at > deadline tells them apart.
